title: When does a smartphone become too old to receive updates?

lines.text: Why do phone manufacturers suddenly stop sending software updates to perfectly working older phones?
It is not just a greedy plan to force you to buy a new device.
lines.caps: Not just a trick to make you *buy | a new *phone!

lines.text: The real bottleneck is the chipset manufacturer who built the processor inside your phone.
lines.caps: The bottleneck is the *chipmaker | who built the *processor

lines.text: Companies like Qualcomm only support driver patches for their microchips for four to five years.
Newer operating systems require modern neural engines, larger RAM, and advanced GPU instruction sets.
lines.caps: New OS features need *advanced | neural hardware and *RAM

lines.text: Without chipmaker driver support, installing new updates would cause phones to lag, overheat, and crash.
lines.caps: Without drivers, new updates would *overheat | and brick the *phone!

lines.text: Once updates stop, unpatched security vulnerabilities make it time for a phone upgrade.
